statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 10% while Stress is extreme at 80%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. NQ futures trade at 29,430.25, down 0.06%, in the middle of a 29,364.00-29,480.25 overnight band worth about 0.40%, after the overnight low was rejected. That is retracement behaviour rather than the persistent no-pullback structure that defines tail conditions, and VIX at 16.46 shows no tail-risk repricing in options. Stress stays extreme because Brent above $101, a 10-year near 4.84% at its highest since 2023, an active tanker conflict in the Gulf and back-to-back PPI and CPI releases make the environment difficult even where mean reversion is intact. A narrow danger window is published around the 12:30 UTC producer price release and the 13:30 UTC cash open.
headline: NQ futures hold 29,430.25, down 0.06%, mid-band after rejecting the 29,364.00 overnight low, while Brent above $101 and a 4.84% 10-year keep Stress extreme into the 12:30 UTC PPI release
body: Observed evidence at the assessment cutoff: Nasdaq-100 E-mini futures print 29,430.25, down 18.50 points or 0.06%, inside an overnight range of 29,364.00 to 29,480.25. That band spans roughly 0.40% and price sits near its middle, having rejected the low rather than extending from it. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 0.29%, within a 29,334.40 to 29,563.60 range. Asian equities are weaker, with MSCI's Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index, the Nikkei and the KOSPI each down about 1%, yet that weakness has not transmitted into directional NQ structure. Cross-asset conditions remain restrictive. Brent trades at $101.00 and WTI at $96.06, both near multi-month highs, after US and Iranian forces exchanged strikes on shipping and Strait of Hormuz transits collapsed to single digits from roughly 125 large vessels a day. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.84%, its highest since 2023, with the 2-year at about 4.39%. VIX at 16.46 is the notable counterweight: implied volatility is not pricing a discontinuity. The scheduled path is dense. August producer prices and weekly jobless claims are released at 12:30 UTC today, with consensus at +0.4% month-on-month headline and +0.3% core, followed by August consumer prices at 12:30 UTC on 11 September and the 15-16 September FOMC meeting, where futures imply roughly 60% odds of a rate increase. Consistent with the standing method, an unreleased number raises Stress and uncertainty rather than observed Tail; only the price path after a release can establish tail conditions. Tail is therefore held at 10% and Stress at 80%. Confidence is 88% on live futures, index, yield, oil and volatility readings alongside a calendar corroborated across independent sources.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 04:00 UTC the mapped policy state was EA_ON in 22 of the 23 available slots, with one WATCH hour at 12:00 UTC on 9 September when Tail reached 20% during a trend-down European session. Tail ranged from 7% to 20% and settled back into a 8-11% band overnight as retracements returned. Stress climbed from 74% to a sustained 80-83% as Brent broke $100 and the 10-year set fresh 2023 highs. The 10:00 UTC slot on 9 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The published conditional path keeps Tail in a 10-14% range through the Asian and European sessions, lifts it to a peak of 22% in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-PPI repricing overlaps the US cash open, and returns it to 10-13% overnight into the CPI session. Only the 12:00 and 13:00 UTC slots map to WATCH; no slot reaches the 25% block threshold on current evidence. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout because oil above $100, a 2023-high 10-year and an active Gulf conflict are regime features that a single release does not clear. Confidence decays from 88% to 81% across the horizon as slots move further beyond the observed sample. A narrow danger window is published from 12:25 to 14:00 UTC.
